root_cause.text: The MPTCP sockopt code in net/mptcp/sockopt.c wrongly used atomic-context lock_sock_fast() to protect subflow sockets while calling sock_set_timestamp() and sock_set_timestamping(), even though those helpers can sleep, causing a scheduling-while-atomic bug.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “Using lock_sock_fast() (atomic context) around sock_set_timestamp() and sock_set_timestamping() is unsafe, as both helpers can sleep,” and the patch fixes this by replacing lock_sock_fast()/unlock_sock_fast() with the sleepable lock_sock()/release_sock() in mptcp_setsockopt_sol_socket_tstamp() and mptcp_setsockopt_sol_socket_timestamping().

intent_record.intent_summary: Use regular socket locking for subflow timestamp option updates to ensure correct locking behavior when propagating the setting across MPTCP subflows.
intent_record.what: Within mptcp_setsockopt_sol_socket_tstamp(), the per-subflow locking was changed from using lock_sock_fast()/unlock_sock_fast() with a saved boolean state to using lock_sock()/release_sock() directly around sock_set_timestamp().
intent_record.how: At runtime, each subflow socket is now always acquired and released with the standard socket lock path instead of the fast-lock helper, which changes the locking behavior used while updating timestamp settings on subflow sockets and avoids relying on the fast-lock state tracking for this operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use regular socket locking for subflow timestamping updates to ensure correct synchronization when applying the option.
intent_record.what: Within mptcp_setsockopt_sol_socket_timestamping(), the per-subflow socket locking was changed from using lock_sock_fast()/unlock_sock_fast() with a saved bool slow variable to using lock_sock()/release_sock() directly around sock_set_timestamping().
intent_record.how: At runtime, each subflow socket now always takes the regular socket lock path before updating timestamping options and releases it with the standard unlock routine, avoiding the fast-lock variant and ensuring the operation is performed under the normal socket locking semantics.

grouping_result.intent: Use regular socket locking for subflow timestamping updates to ensure correct synchronization when applying the option.

consistency_review.core_intent: Use standard socket locking when updating timestamp-related socket options across MPTCP subflows to ensure correct synchronization.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly replace the inappropriate atomic-context fast socket locking with regular socket locking when calling timestamp and timestamping helpers on MPTCP subflows, which matches the root cause of the scheduling-while-atomic bug.

candidates.rationale: This takes the subflow socket with the atomic-context fast lock, and the protected region immediately calls sock_set_timestamp(), which can sleep. Using lock_sock_fast() here is the direct cause of the scheduling-while-atomic bug.

This uses the atomic-context fast socket lock before calling sock_set_timestamping(), a helper that can sleep. That mismatch between lock context and sleeping operation directly embodies the vulnerability.
This helper can sleep, so invoking it while the subflow socket is held with lock_sock_fast() triggers the scheduling-while-atomic condition.
This helper may sleep, and it is executed under lock_sock_fast() in the pre-fix code, making it part of the vulnerable statement sequence.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the primary vulnerable statement because it acquires the subflow socket with the atomic-context fast lock, and the protected region then calls helpers that can sleep. That lock/context mismatch is the root cause of the scheduling-while-atomic bug.
